newsitem.title: USA: Chase's Lieberman leaves to launch hedge fund.
newsitem.headline: Chase's Lieberman leaves to launch hedge fund.

text.p: Veteran Wall Street economist Charles Lieberman said Thursday that he is leaving Chase Securities to form a hedge fund with three other people.
Lieberman will join with fellow Chase economist Sally Kleinman, economist Henry Kaufman and Joseph Oricoli in starting a hedge fund in New York City called Stategic Partners GP LLC.
Hedge funds are highly leveraged, aggressively managed investment funds typically backed by a small number of individual investors.
"We are going to play to our strengths," Lieberman said. "The group is high-powered, and we have a high-quality analytical group. We are going to use that to anticipate market development."
"It's something I have been thinking about for a long time," Lieberman added.

The new fund will concentrate on the United States, but will also be oriented toward the other G7 economies, the group of wealthy industrial nations that includes Japan, France, Germany, Britain, Canada, and Italy, in addition to the United States.
Lieberman, currently chief economist at Chase, will be managing partner at the new firm and handle a combination of economics, strategy and investing.
Kleinman will be head of research, Kaufman will run strategy, and Oricoli will run trading operations at the new firm.
